page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It utilizes the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. This server does not include local storage or discrete graphics processing units.

A key differentiator of this instance is its baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps, designed for network-intensive workloads. In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core performance and software compilation tasks. Memory performance is highly efficient, with Passmark memory scores and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth registering in the top tiers. Single-core performance and cryptographic operations align with average baseline expectations, while database operations and Redis SET throughput show strong performance.

Given its bare-metal architecture and high-density DDR5 memory configuration, the c7gn.metal offers high resource efficiency for multi-threaded, network-bound applications. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is supported by the high-capacity 200 Gbps network interface. This server is highly suited for high-performance computing, software compilation, static web serving at scale, and network-intensive distributed database workloads.
